messages.subject: seq_along question
parts:
Hi:
Could someone help me figure out how to plot some predicted values
into the future when the sequence along the x axis is every 7 days.
The example below works well if the sequence doens't skip any weeks in
between.
weightData <- data.frame(weight = c(2.1,2.4,2.8,3.6,4.1,5.2,6.3),week
= 1:7)
weight <- as.numeric(weightData$weight)
predicted <- forecast(weight,h=3,level=95) # see the predicted
values by forecast
# predicted
# str(predicted)
forecast <- with(predicted, data.frame(
weight = as.numeric(mean),
upper = as.numeric(upper),
lower = as.numeric(lower),
week = length(x) + seq_along(mean)))
forecast
predictValues <-ggplot(weightData, aes(week, weight)) + geom_line
(colour="pink",size=1) + geom_point(size=3,colour="grey45")
predictValues <- predictValues + geom_point
(data=forecast,size=5,colour='green') +
geom_text(data=forecast,label=round(forecast$weight,
1),vjust=2,size=3,colour="blue")
print(predictValues)

But now I want to predict the values after day 49 for days 56,63 and
70 but my graph gets all weird because is trying to plot predicted
values for 8,9 and 10. I have played around a little bit with levels
but I just couldn't make it work. I want my X axis to show days
7,14,21,28,35,42,49 plus the predicted values for days 56,63 and 70
(every 7 days).

weightData <- data.frame(weight = c(2.1,2.4,2.8,3.6,4.1,5.2,6.3),Days=c
(7,14,21,28,35,42,49))
weight <- as.numeric(weightData$weight)
predicted <- forecast(weight,h=3,level=95) # see the predicted
values by forecast
# predicted
# str(predicted)
forecast <- with(predicted, data.frame(
weight = as.numeric(mean),
upper = as.numeric(upper),
lower = as.numeric(lower),
Days = length(x) + seq_along(mean)))
forecast
predictValues <-ggplot(weightData, aes(Days, weight)) + geom_line
(colour="pink",size=1) + geom_point(size=3,colour="grey45")
predictValues <- predictValues + geom_point
(data=forecast,size=5,colour='green') +
geom_text(data=forecast,label=round(forecast$weight,
1),vjust=2,size=3,colour="blue")
print(predictValues)

try the following script:
- changed how the Days are calculated in the forecast dataframe
- x-axis breaks are added manually

===
weightData <- data.frame(weight = c

(2.1,2.4,2.8,3.6,4.1,5.2,6.3),Days=c
(7,14,21,28,35,42,49))
weight <- as.numeric(weightData$weight)
predicted <- forecast(weight,h=3,level=95) # see the predicted values
by forecast
#predicted
# str(predicted)
forecast <- with(predicted, data.frame(
weight = as.numeric(mean),
upper = as.numeric(upper),
lower = as.numeric(lower),

Days = seq(max(weightData)+7, by=7, length.out=length(mean)))) ##
Change in formula

forecast
predictValues <-ggplot(weightData, aes(Days, weight)) + geom_line
(colour="pink",size=1) + geom_point(size=3,colour="grey45")
predictValues <- predictValues + geom_point
(data=forecast,size=5,colour='green') +
geom_text(data=forecast,label=round(forecast$weight,
1),vjust=2,size=3,colour="blue")

predictValues + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(7, by=7, length.out=10))
## Manual breaks

Thanks for the quick reply, It works nicely now. I also tried to
predict the values along the X axis and this is what I came out with:
library(ggplot2)
library(forecast)

Ypredict <- forecast(weight,h=3,level=95) # see the predicted values
by forecast
Xpredict <- forecast(weightData$Days,h=3,level=95)
str(Xpredict)
weight <- as.numeric(Ypredict$mean)
upper <- as.numeric(Ypredict$upper)
lower <- as.numeric(Ypredict$lower)
Days <- Xpredict$mean # IMPORTANT: This variable must have the same
name as the variable from the dataset; in
# this case it should be 'Days'
because the X axis can't read two different variables.
forecast <- data.frame(weight,upper,lower,Days)
weightData$upper <- weightData$weight
weightData$lower <- weightData$weight
both <- rbind(weightData, forecast)
predict2 <- ggplot(both, aes(Days, weight)) + geom_line
(colour="pink",size=1) + geom_point(size=3,colour="grey")
predict2 <- predict2 + geom_smooth(aes(ymin = lower, ymax =
upper),stat = "identity",colour = "pink", fill = "yellow")
predict2 <- predict2 + geom_text(data=forecast,label=round(forecast
$weight,1),vjust=1.5,hjust=-0.1,size=3,colour="blue") +
geom_line(data=forecast,colour="green",size=2) +
geom_point(data=forecast,size=5,colour="hotpink")
print(predict2)

I just hope that is statistically correct to predict X axis values,
but by doing it this way I don't have to hardcode the sequence of my X
values.
